$comment: Residential lease. Jurisdiction-neutral drafting only: every place regulates tenancy differently (deposit caps, notice periods, entry rules, late-charge limits), so anywhere a number is a legal judgement it is left as a [bracketed blank] for the user to fill after checking locally — the rationale says so. Nothing here asserts what any law requires.

clauses.title: Parties and Premises
clauses.rationale: Names who is renting what. Everything else in the lease hangs off these three defined terms.
clauses.body: This Residential Lease Agreement is entered into as of {{date}} between {{company}} (“Landlord”) and {{tenantName}} (“Tenant”). Landlord rents to Tenant the residential premises at {{propertyAddress}} (the “Premises”), together with any furnishings and fixtures listed in an attached inventory.

clauses.title: Occupants
clauses.rationale: Limits who may live in the Premises, so a lease to one person does not quietly become a lease to five. Guests are addressed separately from occupants.
clauses.body: Only Tenant and the following persons may occupy the Premises as their residence: [names of additional occupants, or “none”]. Guests may stay up to [14] days in any six-month period without Landlord’s written consent.

clauses.title: Term of the Tenancy
clauses.rationale: A fixed term gives both sides a known end date. The start date is left blank because leases are usually signed before they begin.
clauses.body: The tenancy is for a fixed term of twelve (12) months, beginning on [start date] and ending on [end date]. If Tenant remains in possession after the end date with Landlord’s consent, the tenancy continues month-to-month on the same terms until either party ends it with at least [30] days’ written notice.

clauses.title: Term of the Tenancy
clauses.rationale: A fixed term gives both sides a known end date. The start date is left blank because leases are usually signed before they begin.
clauses.body: The tenancy is for a fixed term of six (6) months, beginning on [start date] and ending on [end date]. If Tenant remains in possession after the end date with Landlord’s consent, the tenancy continues month-to-month on the same terms until either party ends it with at least [30] days’ written notice.

clauses.title: Term of the Tenancy
clauses.rationale: A fixed term gives both sides a known end date. The start date is left blank because leases are usually signed before they begin.
clauses.body: The tenancy is for a fixed term of twenty-four (24) months, beginning on [start date] and ending on [end date]. If Tenant remains in possession after the end date with Landlord’s consent, the tenancy continues month-to-month on the same terms until either party ends it with at least [30] days’ written notice.

clauses.title: Term of the Tenancy
clauses.rationale: Month-to-month trades certainty for flexibility: either side can end the tenancy on notice. Minimum notice periods differ from place to place, which is why the number is a blank to check locally rather than a default.
clauses.body: The tenancy is month-to-month, beginning on [start date] and continuing until either party ends it with at least [30] days’ written notice to the other.

clauses.title: Rent
clauses.rationale: The amount comes from the wizard; the due day and payment method are drafting choices left visible so the user makes them deliberately.
clauses.body: Tenant will pay Landlord rent of {{monthlyRent}} per month, due in advance on the [1st] day of each month, by [payment method — e.g. bank transfer to the account Landlord designates]. Rent for any partial month at the start or end of the tenancy is prorated by the day.

clauses.title: Late Charges and Returned Payments
clauses.rationale: Offered rather than automatic because many places limit late charges and grace periods — both numbers are the user’s to set after checking what applies where the property is.
clauses.body: If Landlord has not received rent within [number] days after it is due, Tenant will pay a late charge of [amount or percentage]. If any payment is returned unpaid, Tenant will pay Landlord’s returned-payment cost of [amount] and thereafter pay by [certified funds or another method Landlord reasonably specifies].

clauses.title: Security Deposit
clauses.rationale: Included only when the wizard answer names a deposit. Deposit caps, holding rules, and return deadlines differ from place to place, so the return window is a blank to check locally.
clauses.body: Tenant will pay a security deposit of {{securityDeposit}} on or before the start date, held by Landlord as security for Tenant’s performance of this Residential Lease Agreement. Within [number] days after the tenancy ends and Tenant returns possession, Landlord will return the deposit less any amounts properly withheld for unpaid rent or for damage beyond normal wear and tear, with an itemized written statement of anything withheld. The deposit is not a substitute for the last month’s rent.

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.rationale: The two utilities clauses are mutually exclusive on the wizard answer; the exceptions line is left visible so unusual arrangements (e.g. tenant pays only electricity) are a one-word edit.
clauses.body: Rent includes the following utilities and services: [water, sewer, trash, gas, electricity — edit to match]. Tenant is responsible for any utility or service not listed, including [internet and telephone].

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.rationale: The two utilities clauses are mutually exclusive on the wizard answer; the exceptions line is left visible so unusual arrangements are a one-word edit.
clauses.body: Tenant will arrange and pay for all utilities and services to the Premises, including [water, sewer, trash, gas, electricity, internet — edit to match], except the following, which Landlord provides: [none]. Tenant will keep utility accounts in Tenant’s name current through the end of the tenancy.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Use of the Premises
clauses.rationale: Keeps a home a home: the premises are for living in, not for running a storefront out of. The home-office sentence reflects how people actually live and work.
clauses.body: Tenant will use the Premises only as a private residence. Ordinary remote work from home is not a violation of this section; operating a business that brings customers, employees, inventory, or signage onto the Premises requires Landlord’s prior written consent. Tenant will not use the Premises for any unlawful purpose or in a way that unreasonably disturbs neighbors.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Maintenance and Repairs
clauses.rationale: Splits upkeep the way most tenancies do: structure and systems on the landlord, cleanliness and prompt reporting on the tenant. Prompt reporting protects both sides — small leaks are cheap and big ones are not.
clauses.body: Landlord will keep the structure of the Premises and its plumbing, electrical, heating, and supplied appliances in good working repair. Tenant will keep the Premises clean and sanitary, use its systems and appliances reasonably, and promptly notify Landlord in writing of any condition needing repair. Tenant is responsible for damage caused by Tenant, occupants, guests, or pets, beyond normal wear and tear.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Alterations
clauses.rationale: Offered, not automatic — some landlords are happy with paint and shelves, and the clause reads strictly.
clauses.body: Tenant will not make alterations to the Premises — including painting, wallpaper, and fixtures attached to walls or ceilings — without Landlord’s prior written consent. Small picture hooks and ordinary hanging hardware are permitted if holes are repaired at move-out. Approved alterations become part of the Premises unless the parties agree in writing that Tenant may or must remove them.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Pets
clauses.rationale: The permissive variant still names the pets, because “pets allowed” without a description becomes “any number of any animal”. Assistance animals are a separate topic the clause deliberately does not try to cover.
clauses.body: Tenant may keep the following pets at the Premises: [number and description — e.g. one cat]. Tenant will clean up after pets, prevent them from disturbing neighbors, and is responsible for any damage they cause. Additional or replacement pets require Landlord’s prior written consent. [Optional: a pet deposit of [amount], handled the same way as the security deposit.]

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Pets
clauses.rationale: The restrictive variant. Assistance animals are a separate topic the clause deliberately does not try to cover — treating them as “pets” is a mistake this template should not invite.
clauses.body: Tenant will not keep animals at the Premises without Landlord’s prior written consent. This section is not intended to address assistance animals, which the parties will discuss separately if the need arises.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Smoking
clauses.rationale: Offered because it is common, not because it is assumed — the user decides the policy and can soften it to designated outdoor areas.
clauses.body: Smoking and vaping are not permitted inside the Premises or in shared indoor areas. [Optional: smoking is permitted only in the following outdoor area: [describe].] Damage attributable to smoking is damage beyond normal wear and tear.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Landlord’s Entry
clauses.rationale: Balances access with privacy. The notice period is a blank because minimum notice rules differ from place to place and the number is a legal judgement, not a drafting one.
clauses.body: Landlord may enter the Premises to inspect, make repairs, or show it to prospective tenants or buyers, after giving Tenant at least [24 hours’] written notice and entering at reasonable times. No advance notice is needed in an emergency threatening life or property, or if Tenant asks Landlord to enter.

clauses.group: Use and Care of the Premises
clauses.title: Assignment and Subletting
clauses.rationale: Offered because short-term-rental platforms made this the clause landlords most wish they had included. The consent standard is left as a visible choice.
clauses.body: Tenant will not assign this Residential Lease Agreement, sublet the Premises, or offer the Premises or any part of it for short-term stays (including through rental platforms) without Landlord’s prior written consent[, which Landlord will not unreasonably withhold].

clauses.title: Holding Over
clauses.rationale: Only offered for fixed terms — a month-to-month tenancy cannot be held over. Answers the question every fixed-term lease eventually faces: what happens if nobody moves.
clauses.body: If Tenant remains in possession after the fixed term ends without a new written agreement, the tenancy continues month-to-month on the same terms, at a monthly rent of [same rent, or a stated holdover rent], and either party may end it with at least [30] days’ written notice.

clauses.title: Move-Out Condition
clauses.rationale: Sets the end-of-tenancy expectations next to the deposit clause they interact with, so “normal wear and tear” is used the same way in both.
clauses.body: At the end of the tenancy, Tenant will return all keys and access devices, remove all personal belongings and trash, and leave the Premises in the condition received, normal wear and tear excepted. The parties may conduct a joint move-out inspection if either requests one, and Tenant may provide a forwarding address for the return of any deposit.
